items.title: After Two Decades, U.S. Forces Leave Iraq to an Uncertain Future
items.summary: Some Iraqis are celebrating the end of an American military presence that unleashed waves of bloodshed. Others fear what happens next for their country, trapped between Washington and Tehran.

items.title: Live Updates: Pilot May Have Attempted to Crash Flight to Israel, Netanyahu Says
items.summary: Passengers intervened and “prevented a disaster” after one pilot stabbed another during a flight from Dubai, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said. The plane landed safely in Saudi Arabia. The motive for the attack was not clear.

items.title: A Way Out of the A.I. Arms Race?
items.summary: New research points to how the world could stop short of the brink of disaster. Even with the agreement signed at the White House by tech leaders, it won’t be easy.

items.title: American Forces Withdraw From Iraq 23 Years After Invading
items.summary: The Americans did not understand the country when they invaded in 2003. Over a correspondent’s many trips there, it was not clear that this ever changed much.

items.title: Moth Swarms Sweep Across Australia. That’s Good News.
items.summary: Bogong moths have been in decline since the 1980s, but this spring the insects have been sighted in the thousands across southeastern Australia, delighting scientists.

items.title: In Fractious France, Politicians Agree on One Thing: Pope Leo Was a Hit
items.summary: In a four-day visit, Pope Leo XIV won praise across the political spectrum, even from its most avowedly secular figures.

items.title: Israeli Settlers Stop Soldiers From Returning Palestinians to Their Home
items.summary: The Supreme Court had ordered the military to ensure a West Bank family that fled violence could go back. But settlers blocked the effort, with the authorities accused of not doing enough to confront them.

items.title: No Bombs Found in U.K. Case, but Officials Say Threat to Bases Is Real
items.summary: The prospect of an attack on an air base used by U.S. forces prompted stepped-up protections across Europe, but confusion shrouds the case, in which the suspects were released on bail.

items.title: Why the U.S. Is Imposing New Visa Restrictions on South Africa
items.summary: The Trump administration announced new visa restrictions on the country days after receiving a letter that South African officials had hoped would bring down the temperature.

items.title: Bomb by Bomb, the Slow Death of My Hometown in Ukraine
items.summary: It was possible, for a time, to think that Kramatorsk, where I was born and raised, would survive the war mostly unscathed. Not any more.

items.title: Condé Nast C.E.O. Leaves to Run Mattel
items.summary: Roger Lynch, who has led the publisher for more than seven years, will become the chief executive of the toy company, he said Wednesday.

items.title: Fed’s Preferred Inflation Gauge Points to Continued Price Pressures
items.summary: The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index showed little sign of easing in August, though revised data showed inflation had been slightly cooler than previously believed.

items.title: Bracing for More Inflation Volatility
items.summary: Consumers, business owners and investors are growing increasingly concerned about rising inflation, and its potential repercussions.

items.title: DeepSeek and Huawei Target a Key Source of Nvidia’s A.I. Dominance
items.summary: In China’s push for self-reliance in artificial intelligence, DeepSeek and Huawei have teamed up to develop software tools for advanced chips.

items.title: Trump’s New Tariffs Face a Familiar Court Challenge
items.summary: For the third time in less than two years, the Trump administration is set to return to court on Wednesday to defend its power to wage a punishing global trade war.

items.title: How to Listen to Your Favorite Music, Online or Off the Grid
items.summary: Streaming services can introduce you to a wonderland of nearly unlimited audio, but downloading your digital collection has advantages.

items.title: He Was a Tech Investor Before There Was a Silicon Valley
items.summary: Bill Draper began funding start-ups in the early 1960s, when the Santa Clara Valley was better known for apricot orchards than microchips. He has died at 98.

items.title: Troubles at Situational Awareness Point to Record Stock Market Leverage
items.summary: A meltdown at Situational Awareness, an A.I.-focused investment firm, is raising tough questions about the Wall Street banks that lent billions to the upstart firm.

items.title: A.I. Is ‘Better Informed’ Than Doctors, Kennedy Tells Industry-Backed MAHA Summit
items.summary: The health secretary, Vice President JD Vance and other top officials addressed a conference sponsored by corporations, including A.I. companies and others with business before the government.

items.title: X2, the Troubled California Six Flags Roller Coaster, Reaches Its End
items.summary: The ride at Magic Mountain near Los Angeles has fueled lawsuits claiming that it had caused brain injuries, including two that were fatal.

items.title: How Meta Uses A.I. Data Centers to Avoid Billions in Federal Taxes
items.summary: Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research and experimentation. Its own accountants say the gambit is risky.

items.title: At A.I. Event, Trump Asks Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft to Make Safety Decisions Themselves
items.summary: President Trump’s meetings with tech leaders produced some voluntary safeguards and a commitment to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” the term that Mr. Trump prefers.

items.title: OpenAI Ignored Employees’ Warnings About Safely Testing A.I. Models
items.summary: Employees and security researchers said that they had cautioned the company on safely testing its A.I. models and strengthening its corporate infrastructure, but that OpenAI did not listen.

items.title: Ukrainian Science Academy, Struck by Drone, Played Key Role in Research
items.summary: Over 90 percent of Ukraine’s scientific discoveries have been attributed to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences, including advancements in astronomy and military technology.

items.title: OpenAI Unveils Dots, New A.I. Agents to Rival Meta’s Muse
items.summary: The ChatGPT maker unveiled agents that act as assistants, just weeks after Meta released Muse, as it faces scrutiny over incidents involving its technology.

items.title: Is Claude Conscious? Inside Anthropic’s Quest to Instill Morality Into Its A.I. Models
items.summary: In a series of private meetings, the company consulted religious scholars to help instill morality into its A.I. models — and make the case that Claude could be conscious.

items.title: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
items.summary: Dorm Room Fund, a program that lets college students invest in their peers, raised a new $50 million fund as the competition for young founders ramps up.

items.title: OpenAI Says It Will Not Release Newest Astra A.I. Model Over Safety Concerns
items.summary: The company’s researchers raised questions about the security of the model, known as GPT-6.1 Astra.
